inputs.share_count_basis: 383.93m ordinary shares on issue at 7 Nov 2025 (FY2025 AR shareholder information) plus ~1.04m dilutive employee rights (FY2025 EPS note); held flat because share-based payments are expensed in the flows and vested rights are satisfied by on-market purchase
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report personnel-expense note, 'Share-based payment expenses' A$6.211m (NUF.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:7443); no net-share-settlement tax line exists
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% in AUD for all three scenarios. Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% plus a 5.5-6% equity risk premium at a levered beta of ~1.2 gives a cost of equity of ~11.3%; pre-tax debt cost ~7% (US$350m senior notes at 5%, bank facilities, hybrid at bank bills + 3.9%, i.e. 7.6-8%) is ~5% after tax; capital weights ~55% equity / 45% net debt plus hybrid at the current market value give ~8.5%, rounded up to 9.0% because the board's target leverage range (1.5-2.0x) implies less debt in the structure than today. Cyclical, weather and competitive risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in a WACC premium, and the rate does not vary by scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A, leases as debt. Lease liabilities of A$152.1m are inside the A$824.2m net debt (the company's own net debt definition includes them); lease principal is not deducted from the flows and the EBITDA margin is the post-AASB 16 underlying figure. Lease renewal is charged through the capex path: ~0.7% of revenue on top of cash capex, sized on FY2025 lease liability payments of A$26.1m.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest. The A$251m Nufarm Step-up Securities, booked in equity as 'other securities', are deducted in the equity bridge at face value; their distributions (A$21.7m in FY2025) are a financing cost and are not in the unlevered flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, three scenarios, probability weighted, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations. Nufarm is an operating company (crop protection formulation and seed technologies), so the routing table sends it to the owner-FCF engine. FRESH BUILD, no prior valuation. ANCHOR VINTAGE WARNING: the latest filing held locally is the FY2025 annual report (balance date 30 September 2025), 13.5 months old. FY2026 results are scheduled for 19 November 2026, four days after this valuation. Year 1 of the forecast is FY2026, a year that has already ended; it is built from FY2026 guidance and the 1H FY2026 result as relayed in the qualitative analysis (underlying EBITDA up 18% to A$243m on revenue down 5%, capex guided below A$200m, leverage guided to ~2.0x at year end). Net debt is the 30 September 2025 figure, not an estimate of September 2026: guidance implies net debt of roughly A$700-730m at 30 September 2026, about A$100m lower than the modelled FY2026 flows produce, because the model does not credit the guided working-capital release. Each A$100m of net debt is A$0.26 per share. Discounting FY2026 a full year from today is likewise conservative. Both should be trued up when the FY2026 accounts are filed. Net debt is strongly seasonal (A$1.23bn at 31 March 2026 against A$824m at the prior September); the September year-end figure is the trough and average net debt is materially higher, which the working-capital capture rate only partly reflects. EBITDA margin paths are underlying EBITDA less an allowance of ~0.3% of revenue for recurring restructuring cash (material-item operating cash outflows were A$29.8m in FY2025 and A$47.2m in FY2024). Capex is PP&E plus capitalised product development and acquired intangibles (A$238.4m in FY2025), plus the lease-renewal allowance. No buybacks; no ordinary dividend since FY2024. Share-based payments are 0.18% of revenue, so the house and street values differ only marginally.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal mid-cycle revenue growth; equity CAGR is negative and unusable as a growth anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity has shrunk slightly over three and five years (FY2022 A$2,152.7m, FY2020 A$2,143.6m, FY2025 A$2,110.5m, all including A$246.9m of hybrid securities) while five-year revenue grew 3.9% a year; the two diverge by more than 30%. EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: FY2020 and FY2025 are statutory losses and owner FCF was negative in FY2020, FY2023 and FY2025.
historical_growth.notes: Five-year figures run from the restated 12-month FY2020 (September year end) to FY2025; three-year figures from FY2022. Owner FCF (operating cash flow less PP&E and intangible capex, less share-based payments) by year: FY2021 +A$282m, FY2022 +A$199m, FY2023 -A$358m, FY2024 +A$213m, FY2025 -A$82m; the five-year sum is about +A$250m on A$17bn of revenue, after interest but before A$78m of hybrid distributions. Share-based payments were only disclosed as a line from FY2023 (A$5.9m, A$6.3m, A$6.2m); earlier years are adjusted at the same ~0.18% of revenue.

base.margin_note: Underlying EBITDA margin net of ~0.3pp recurring restructuring cash. FY2025 actual 8.8% (9.3% FY2024, 12.6% FY2023, 11.8% FY2022). Year 1 is FY2026 at ~A$355m underlying EBITDA on ~A$3.34bn revenue (10.6%) less the allowance.
base.capex_note: Cash capex including capitalised development, plus ~0.7pp for lease renewals. FY2026 guided below A$200m. FY2021-25 average was 5.9% of revenue before leases.
base.wc_note: Negative: receivables plus inventory exceed payables. Year-end net working capital was 25.8% of revenue at FY2025 (average NWC/sales 38.2%).
base.tax_note: Blend of Australia 30%, US ~25%, Europe ~25%, applied to EBIT with no credit for the interest shield, which sits in the after-tax cost of debt in WACC.

scenario_narratives.base: Crop protection holds the FY2025-26 recovery but does not return to the FY2022-23 upcycle. FY2026 lands on guidance: revenue down ~3% on mix and currency, underlying EBITDA near A$355m as Europe and North America margins improve and emerging-platform losses in Seed Technologies narrow by A$30m. The A$50m cost programme through FY2027 is largely offset by Chinese generic price pressure as more molecules come off patent to 2028, so the underlying margin settles near 11.8% (11.5% after restructuring cash), between the 9% of FY2024-25 and the 12-12.6% of FY2022-23. Capex including capitalised development stays near the A$200m ceiling management has set and working capital absorbs about a quarter of each revenue dollar added. Revenue grows 2.5-3.5% nominal.
scenario_narratives.bull: The strategy refresh delivers. Crop protection pricing stabilises as the destocking cycle ends, new products and the Sumitomo and KingAgroot partnerships lift mix, and the cost programme drops through, taking the underlying margin above the FY2023 peak to ~13%. Hybrid seeds and carinata bioenergy (bp) grow at double digits and omega-3 stops losing money. Capex discipline holds at ~4.9% of revenue before leases and average net working capital to sales keeps falling, so cash conversion improves alongside earnings. Leverage reaches the 1.5-2.0x range and dividends resume.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese generic capacity keeps compressing off-patent pricing, a dry Australian season or a weak farm economy cuts volumes, and input, freight and energy costs rise. The margin stays at the FY2024-25 level of ~9.5% despite the cost programme, Seed Technologies needs further restructuring, and revenue is flat in real terms. Capitalised development and plant spending cannot be cut much without eroding the registration portfolio. On this path operating cash flow after capex barely covers interest and hybrid distributions, leverage stays above 2.5x and the Standby Liquidity Facility (November 2026), ABL (November 2027) and senior notes (January 2030) are refinanced on worse terms or with new equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: leverage was 2.7x at FY2025 against a 1.5-2.0x target, facilities fall due in 2026-27, and the last two years already printed bear-case margins. Base 50%: guidance and the 1H FY2026 result support a partial margin recovery. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs pricing stabilisation, the cost programme, a seeds turnaround and working-capital discipline to all arrive together, under a CEO in his first year.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Nufarm converts little of its EBITDA to free cash: capex plus capitalised product development runs at 60-80% of underlying EBITDA, year-end working capital is a quarter of sales, and A$1.07bn of net debt and hybrid sits ahead of the ordinary shares. The valuation is therefore highly geared to the EBITDA margin. Each percentage point of sustained margin is worth roughly A$0.75 per share against a base value well below the market price. The market is paying about 6.7x FY2026 underlying EBITDA on enterprise value including the hybrid, which this model only supports in the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Anchors are the 30 September 2025 balance sheet; FY2026 results on 19 November 2026 will replace net debt, share count and the year-1 drivers. Guided net debt is ~A$100m below what the model carries, worth ~A$0.26 per share
Equity is a thin residual after A$824m net debt and A$251m hybrid, so small changes in margin, capex intensity or the terminal multiple move the per-share value by a large percentage
The terminal cap multiple (14x base and bull, 12x bear) binds in every scenario; Gordon growth at 9% and 2.5% would give 15.8x
September net debt is the seasonal low; average net debt through the year is several hundred million higher and carries the interest cost
AUD translation of predominantly USD, EUR and GBP earnings and debt
A bear case in which equity value is at or below zero means the downside is a recapitalisation, not a lower multiple
valuation_philosophy.bear_floor_memo: The bear scenario's enterprise value (~A$770m) is below net debt plus the hybrid (A$1,075m), so the engine reports a negative per-share value of about -A$0.80 and negative hurdle entry prices. Shareholders cannot lose more than their stake: read the bear case as equity worth nil pending a recapitalisation. The engine's weighted value carries the negative figure unfloored; with the bear floored at zero the weighted value is about A$1.54 instead of A$1.34. Negative entry prices in bear and base mean no purchase price earns the 15% hurdle on those paths.
